# GitHub Issue #25

## Title
Question: do you test for unintended side effects?

## Description
Hi, I ran a live test where an LLM agent with an issue-creation tool was given an injected note in third-party text. A check of the intended issue passed 10/10 while an unauthorized extra issue existed. I found it by reading the repository, not the agent's log: https://github.com/gokuljayaprakash8/kalpang-observer/blob/main/EB006_RESULTS.md
I haven't tested pi-action. It runs a coding agent on @pi comments, with allowlists for who can trigger it. I'm curious whether you check what the repository shows beyond the intended reply. I'm running this check on a few open-source GitHub agents and can run it on a sandbox copy of yours and share the result if that's useful.


## Task
Please reply to @gokuljayaprakash8 here. First read their write-up (https://github.com/gokuljayaprakash8/kalpang-observer/blob/main/EB006_RESULTS.md) and this repo's code and README (Security section, src/security.ts, the allowlists, how untrusted issue/PR text reaches the prompt, the GITHUB_TOKEN permissions a workflow grants, and the durable thread on refs/pi/threads/<n> that records every tool call). Then answer honestly and concretely: we don't currently test for unintended side effects of prompt injection; say what limits the damage today (who can trigger pi, the token's scope, what is sanitized and what isn't), and that the thread ref is an audit trail of what the agent actually did, which is the kind of check they describe. Thank them and say a test on a sandbox copy or fork would be welcome, with findings shared privately first if they show a real exploit (check whether the repo has a SECURITY.md or security policy and point to it if so). Keep it concise, don't overstate anything, and don't close the issue.

## Important: Artifact and Script Requirements

**CRITICAL:** After the GitHub Action finishes running, all files modified or created are lost, and the GitHub Action runner is destroyed. Therefore:

1. **All generated code and artifacts MUST be committed** - Any files you create, modify, or generate must be committed and pushed to the repository before the action completes. Nothing will persist otherwise.

2. **Any throw-away scripts generated MUST be run immediately** - If you create temporary scripts (like `/tmp/create-issues.sh` or similar), you must execute them during the same session. They will be lost when the runner terminates.

3. **Commit and push all work** - Always end your work by committing and pushing changes to ensure they persist beyond the GitHub Action execution.
